events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Wellington
events.description: 1 death. Fairfax County. Hundreds of trees and branches blew down on George Washington Memorial Parkway near Morningside Lane, blocking the roadway for three days. One tree fell onto a vehicle, killing the occupant.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Gum Spgs
events.description: 1 death. Fairfax County. Trees blew down near the intersection of Pole Road and Frye Road, including one onto a vehicle killing the occupant.

events.title: Flash Flood near Greenwood
events.description: 1 death. Albemarle County. Twelve year old boy perished after being swept away by rushing floodwaters in a headwater of Stockton Creek. Stockton Creek was overflowing onto roads and fields several feet deep. Portions of Brooksville Road and Newtown Road were washed out, with water rescues occurring on Brooksville Rd.

events.title: Flash Flood near Holly Brook
events.description: 1 death. Bland County. A vehicle with a single occupant was pushed off of Kimberling Road into deeper water as Kimberling Creek flooded at least 2 feet over the roadway. The occupant attempted to abandon the vehicle, but was swept away by the flooding and passed away. Nearby, Wesendonck Road was observed flooded and impassible at several locations due to multiple creeks overflowing their banks. This includes Nobusiness Creek.

events.title: Flash Flood near Whitetop
events.description: 1 death. Grayson County. Considerable to catastrophic flash flooding occurred across Grayson County. This included at least 200 bridges or culverts that were completely washed out, making the roads impassible. Five large pipes were washed out in the county: three on Route 783 (Helton Creek Lane) and two on Route 749 (Cabin Creek).

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Quioccasin
events.description: 1 death. Henrico County. Law enforcement reported that a tree fell on a car, resulting in a fatality. This was confirmed by broadcast media from Henrico Police and Fire.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Warminster
events.description: 1 death. Nelson County. Nelson County Sheriff confirmed one person died when thunderstorm winds downed a tree limb onto the vehicle they were sheltering in near Wingina.

events.title: Flash Flood near Blackridge
events.description: 1 death. Mecklenburg County. Law Enforcement reported a death in the vicinity of the Tanglewood Shores recreation and boat ramp on the night of January 9, 2024. News articles about the event mention that the individual was driving his golf cart during the heavy rain and was washed away by the rushing creek water. The road where this individual usually drives his golf cart was flooded, leading to this conclusion. The time is estimated from radar.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Minnieville
events.description: 1 death. Prince William County. Trees blew down around Montclair, including one onto a residence in the 15000 block of Holly Hill Drive killing the resident inside.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Vicey
events.description: 1 death. Dickenson County. A tree fell down onto an occuipied vehicle on Welcome Lane near the town of Vicey. The occupant of the car, a sixty-five year old man, died as a result.

events.title: Lightning near Wares Xrds
events.description: 1 death. Louisa County. A 73 year old man was struck and killed by lightning while boating on Lake Anna in Louisa county. Also, a pregnant woman was injured.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Williamsburg
events.description: 1 death. Williamsburg (c) County. Local media reported a tree branch fell onto a moving car causing one fatality and one injury.

events.title: Flash Flood near Kelsa
events.description: 1 death. Buchanan County. Guesses Creek rose out of its banks and led to significant damage of twenty homes around the town of Hurley.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Monroe
events.description: 1 death. Amherst County. Thunderstorm winds blew down a tree directly upon an enclosed trailer. A 34 year old male was loading a lawn mower into the trailer at the time the tree fell, unfortunately, killing him instantly. Damage values are estimated.

events.title: Hail near Lofton
events.description: 1 death. Augusta County. Quarter sized hail accumulated two inches deep on Interstate 81 and Interstate 64 near Spotswood, causing multiple accidents and partially closing the highway. This led to one fatalitiy and five injuries.

events.title: Lightning near Thomastown
events.description: 1 death. Bath County. A 12-year old male went outside to play in a wooden area after rain had stopped falling, and a thunderstorm had moved out of the area. Lightning struck the child. First responders determined that the child did not have a pulse and was not breathing. Air support for medical transport was requested, but was not available due to weather conditions in the area. The child was transported by ambulance to nearby hospital where he was revived by medial staff. The child was transported again by ambulance to a larger hospital. It was at this larger hospital where the child died.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near (bkt)blackstone Aaf
events.description: 1 death. Nottoway County. Large tree was downed during a training exercise at Fort Pickett killing one person and injuring two other people.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Aquia
events.description: 1 death. Stafford County. A tree fell onto a house on Doyle Place, injuring an 82 year old male and killing a 78 year old female who were asleep in the house at the time.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Victoria
events.description: 1 death. Lunenburg County. Multiple trees were downed on the west side of town. A tree fell onto a home resulting in a fatality.

events.title: Flash Flood near Brosville
events.description: 1 death. Pittsylvania County. Pittsylvania County was included in a Presidential Major Disaster declaration due mainly to the severe flooding associated with Tropical Storm Michael. Rainfall of 4 to 8 inches in several hours triggered widespread flash flooding across the county with numerous roads closed and extensive damage. A man lost his life when his automobile was washed off Sandy Creek Road near the 600 block during intense flooding along Sandy Creek. Media reports indicate the incident occurred around 330 PM local time, with one witness observing that water was flowing rapidly at least two feet above the road…

events.title: Flash Flood near Keysville
events.description: 2 deaths. Charlotte County. Charlotte County was included in a Presidential Major Disaster declaration due mainly to the severe flooding associated with Tropical Storm Michael. There was widespread flash flooding across the county with numerous roads closed and damaged. Two people lost their lives after being swept off a bridge into floodwaters. The fatalities occurred after a car stranded on a Mt. Harmony Road bridge around 728 PM local Thursday. The Charlotte County Sheriff's office stated that the vehicle originally had three occupants who were said to be clinging to the bridge railings. A 17-year-old male was able…

events.title: Flash Flood near Danville
events.description: 2 deaths. Danville (c) County. Danville City was included in a Presidential Major Disaster declaration due mainly to the severe flooding associated with Tropical Storm Michael. Catastrophic flash flooding occurred across the City of Danville as extreme rains of 4 to 8 inches in several hours fell. Two people were killed in Danville after being were caught inside vehicles in the floodwaters and were pulled under rising waters as rescuers struggled to reach them. The first was 53-year old man that occurred at 500 PM local time in the 100 block of Colonial Court. The second occurred around 1020 PM on Goodyear Boulevard, as a…

events.title: Tornado near Beach
events.description: 1 death. Chesterfield County. Beginning in Winterpock, the tornado started as a weak EF1 before moving into a residential area north of River Road. The tornado reached peak intensity (EF2) when it crossed Hull Street Road. At this point, it took off the roof of Gabe's and damaged several other businesses. After crossing Hull Street Road, it destroyed the Old Dominion Warehouse, where one person was killed and one was injured. It remained an EF2 until about Gregwood Drive, completely destroying trees and damaging other structures. It then quickly weakened to an EF0 as it reached Powhite Parkway, and continued as an EF0…

events.title: Flood near Roanoke
events.description: 1 death. Roanoke (c) County. A 53-year old woman was reported to have drowned in the Roanoke River during flooding from Florence although details were lacking in terms of location and timing. The Roanoke River at Roanoke (RONV2) crested at 11.41 feet (10,200 cfs) around mid-day on the 17th. Minor flood stage is 10 feet. Several low water bridges and the Roanoke Greenway were flooded and closed. This was the highest stage since September 30, 2015 and was roughly a 2- to 5-year flood event (0.5 - 0.2 annual chance flood).

events.title: Flash Flood near Farmington
events.description: 2 deaths. Albemarle County. Two cars were swept off Old Ballard Road at Ivy Creek. The occupant of one vehicle escaped and was rescued. The second vehicle was observed to repeatedly toss and overturn in the raging floodwaters. The two occupants of that vehicle could not be rescued and were found dead.

events.title: Flash Flood near Syria
events.description: 1 death. Madison County. Two women attempted to cross the swollen Rose River at Graves Mountain Lodge in an ATV. When one of the women got out to check on the water, she was knocked off her feet and swept away. The other woman was uninjured and rescued.

events.title: Lightning near Chesapeake
events.description: 3 deaths (indirect). Chesapeake (c) County. Lightning strike caused a deadly fire at the Chesapeake Senior Living Complex. The fire killed three people and injured six others. There were 68 units that were damaged beyond repair.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Highland Spgs
events.description: 1 death. Henrico County. Large tree limb was downed onto a vehicle on Confederate Run Court.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Saumsville
events.description: 1 death. Shenandoah County. A tree fell onto a pickup truck. One fatality was reported.

events.title: Lightning near Stone Mt
events.description: 1 death. Bedford County. A man was struck by lightning while walking along Highway 122. He later died from his injuries.

events.title: Flood near Parksley
events.description: 1 death. Accomack County. Heavy rainfall from earlier thunderstorms continued to produce numerous reports of flooding and road closures across central Accomack county.

events.title: Tornado near Spring Mills
events.description: 1 death. Appomattox County. A tornado touched down just outside Appomattox county in Campbell county, then traveled 16 miles northeast across Appomattox county. At its peak, this tornado reached EF-3 intensity, which was the first EF-3 tornado or stronger in the month of February in the NWS Blacksburg forecast area. For Appomattox County, this was only the third tornado on record since 1950, and the only tornado rated EF-3 or higher.||The tornado passed just southeast of the town of Appomattox, impacting the community of Evergreen before lifting near Holiday Lake State Park. The fatality and all the injuries occurred in…

events.title: Tornado near Newville
events.description: 3 deaths. Sussex County. NWS storm survey concluded that an EF1 tornado occurred near Waverly. The tornado began a few miles south southwest of Waverly, moved fast through the town of Waverly, then ended about five miles north northeast of Waverly in Surry county. Maximum winds were between 100 and 110 mph. Numerous trees were downed, with two mobile homes destroyed and several homes and businesses damaged.

events.title: Flood near Simmerman
events.description: 1 death. Wythe County. A vehicle with one occupant was washed into Cripple Creek and found later further downstream. The creek was in flood during the overnight and morning hours of April 19-20. The exact time of the incident is unknown but was estimated byto be around 9 AM.

events.title: Flood near Davenport
events.description: 1 death. Buchanan County. Small streams started to flood by evening on the 4th. Guess Fork flooded roads around Hurley. ||Around 2245E on the 4th, a 61 year old man drove his car into flood waters near the mouth of Hurricane Creek with the Russell Fork. This was along Route 80. His car was washed into the water. His body was recovered the next day. A female occupant of the car was able to escape.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Cape Charles
events.description: 3 deaths. Northampton County. Downburst straight line wind damage occurred from the southern portions of Cherrystone Campground southward into Cape Charles, then eastward through Cheriton to Oyster. The most significant damage occurred from Cherrystone Campground eastward to just east of Route 13 in Cheriton and southward to just north of the intersection of Route 13 and Route 184 east of Cape Charles. Numerous trees were downed, snapped off or large limbs were blown out. A couple of trees were downed on homes. Several large camping trailers were overturned in Cherrystone Campground. 3 people died when a tree fell on the…

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Abingdon
events.description: 1 death. Washington County. Broadcast media personnel reported a pedestrian was struck by a falling tree in the 100 block of West Main street in Abingdon. The victim was a 56 year old at the time of the event. At the time of the event the peak wind gusts were only recorded at 24 mph via the CWOP station 1 mile south of Abingdon.

events.title: Flash Flood near Brucetown
events.description: 1 death. Frederick County. Old Charles Town Road was flooded at Opequon Creek.
